events.title: Great Fire of New York
events.description: During the British occupation of New York City in the American Revolutionary War, a fire broke out and destroyed up to 1,000 buildings, a large share of the city.
events.significance: The blaze left much of the city in ruins and remains one of the most destructive fires in early American history.

events.title: The Hobbit is published
events.description: J.R.R. Tolkien's children's fantasy novel about Bilbo Baggins and his unexpected journey was first published in the United Kingdom.
events.significance: The book's success led to The Lord of the Rings and helped shape modern fantasy literature.

events.title: Malta gains independence
events.description: Malta became independent from the United Kingdom after more than 160 years of British rule. At first it kept the British monarch as head of state.
events.significance: Independence began Malta's path as a sovereign nation. It became a republic on December 13, 1974.

events.title: Westgate Mall attack in Nairobi
events.description: Militants from the extremist group al-Shabaab attacked the Westgate shopping mall in Nairobi, Kenya, and a siege followed. At least 63 civilians were killed before Kenyan security forces ended it.
events.significance: The attack was among the deadliest terrorist incidents in Kenya's history and drew global attention to the threat from al-Shabaab.
